Excel, PowerPoint and Word

Source: vignettes/articles/exporting.Rmd
exporting.Rmd

This page shows how to turn the tables and charts you already have into an Excel workbook, a PowerPoint deck and a Word file. For interactive tables, see Interactive charts, tables and apps. The data below is made up.

library(phwstyle)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
use_phw_ggplot()
set.seed(1)
dat <- tibble(group = sample(c("Group A", "Group B", "Group C"), 300, replace = TRUE),
              type = sample(c("Type 1", "Type 2", "Type 3"), 300, replace = TRUE),
              year = sample(2024:2025, 300, replace = TRUE))
tab <- phw_group_table(dat, c(group, type), year)
bars <- ggplot(dat, aes(group, fill = type)) + geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_phw_d() + labs(x = NULL, y = "Cases", fill = NULL)

Excel

phw_write_xlsx() writes one sheet per table, with a title, a navy header, number formats, frozen headers and the source underneath. Summary tables keep their bold group rows and indents.

phw_write_xlsx(list(Grouped = tab, Raw = dat), "tables.xlsx",
               title = c("Counts by group and type", "Raw data"), source = "Example data")
An Excel sheet with a grouped table

PowerPoint

phw_pptx() starts a deck from the PHW template. It is 16:9, with Ubuntu text, navy titles and a navy bar across the top of each content slide. phw_add_slide() adds one slide at a time, and each slide holds a title and one chart, one table or one set of bullet points. Add source and date for the caption at the bottom. Save the deck with print().

deck <- phw_pptx() |>
  phw_add_slide("Weekly summary", text = "Team name, example data",
                layout = "Title Slide") |>
  phw_add_slide("Key messages",
                text = c("First message", "Second message", "Third message")) |>
  phw_add_slide("Cases by group and type", plot = bars,
                source = "Example data", date = "2025-06-30") |>
  phw_add_slide("Grouped table", table = tab, source = "Example data") |>
  phw_add_slide("Next steps", layout = "Section Header")
print(deck, target = "slides.pptx")
Slides from the PHW template: a title slide, bullet points and a chart

Layouts

layout picks a slide layout from the template. The default is "Title and Content". The PHW template also has these:

  • "Title Slide" shows the title on a navy background, with text as the subtitle.
  • "Section Header" shows the title on navy, for the start of a section.
  • "Title Only" and "Blank" leave room for your own content.
  • "Two Content" has two body areas, and phw_add_slide() fills the first.

Charts and tables

Each argument below has a default that suits most slides. Change one only when a slide needs it.

  • plot_scale enlarges the text of a chart on the slide, as a multiple of its size. The default 1.5 brings axis and legend text to about 14 points, and 1 leaves the chart as it is.
  • table_fit enlarges a table built here from a data frame or summary table, by up to 1.6 times for the text, so it reads on a slide. FALSE keeps the size phw_flextable() gives it. A flextable you pass in is never resized.
  • editable adds a chart as an editable vector graphic when the rvg package is installed, so colleagues can change it in PowerPoint. editable = FALSE adds a picture instead.
  • alt gives a chart or table alternative text for screen readers. Without it, a ggplot uses the text from labs(alt = ).
  • caption_args takes a list of phw_caption() arguments other than source and date, such as source_prefix.
deck <- phw_pptx() |>
  phw_add_slide("Cases by group and type", plot = bars,
                alt = "Stacked bars of cases in groups A, B and C, split by type.",
                source = "Example data", caption_args = list(source_prefix = "Data: "),
                plot_scale = 1.5, editable = FALSE)

title_size sets the title size, which is 28 points by default. The title and section slides set their own size, so title_size applies there only when you give it.

Your own template

Pass a PowerPoint file to phw_pptx() to use its layouts instead. Name the layouts it has in layout, and master too, if two slide masters share a layout name. officer::layout_summary() lists them.

The template names Ubuntu without embedding it, so PowerPoint shows it only on computers that have the font. See Installation and setup.

phw_reference_pptx() writes the PHW template to a file. Open it in PowerPoint to see the layouts or to start your own template from it.

phw_reference_pptx("phw-template.pptx")
deck <- phw_pptx("phw-template.pptx")
officer::layout_summary(deck)

The gallery shows slides and Office files.

Word

Any phw_flextable() can be saved to Word, several to one file:

flextable::save_as_docx(`Table 1` = phw_flextable(tab), path = "tables.docx")

See Tables for the other table renderers. For whole reports, use output: phwstyle::phw_word_document in R Markdown or format: phw-docx in Quarto, as Reports, slides and dashboards explains.
